sentences.text: Ferenceratops is identified by a unique set of anatomical features that separate it from other known dinosaurs.
Its shoulder blade is narrow with a strap-like blade and a prominent, upwardly concave acromial process.
The hip bone known as the ischium is gently curved and lacks an obturator process.
No traits typical of ornithopods were found in the holotype, while several characteristics align with ceratopsians.
The genus Ferenceratops was formally established by Maidment and colleagues in 2026.
Fossils originally assigned to this genus were previously referred to the ornithopod Zalmoxes.
The original genus Zalmoxes, which included the species later moved to Ferenceratops, was described in 2003 by Weishampel and colleagues.
The specific name shqiperorum honors the people of Shqiperia, the Albanian name for their nation.
The holotype is a partial skeleton currently housed at the Natural History Museum in London.
Ferenceratops shared its habitat with titanosaurian sauropods and feathered theropods like Balaur and Elopteryx.
The Sânpetru Formation also contained the ankylosaur Struthiosaurus and the hadrosauromorph Telmatosaurus.
The broader fauna included the giant pterosaur Hatzegopteryx, various crocodilians, snakes, lizards, turtles, birds, mammals, amphibians, and fish.
Ferenceratops is classified as a ceratopsian dinosaur.
Researchers placed the animal within the Ceratopsia based on a phylogenetic analysis by Maidment et al. in 2026.
The genus belongs to the parent group Ceratopsia.
It is further classified in the class Ornithischia.
Ferenceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Maastrichtian period.
This corresponds to the Maastrichtian stage, occurring between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
The type locality for the species is the Sânpetru and Densuș-Ciula formations.
These fossils were discovered in Romania.
The environment was subtropical, featuring fluctuating rainy and dry seasons.
It is debated whether material previously assigned to rhabdodontids like Zalmoxes actually belongs to multiple distinct taxa, including both iguanodonts and ceratopsians.
There is ongoing discussion regarding whether Ferenceratops belongs to the Rhabdodontidae or Ceratopsia, as it was traditionally classified as an ornithopod.
